testCases.taskDescription: Verify exception list creation is captured in the audit trail with complete metadata
Check that editing an exception list writes a new immutable audit event.
Verify that list suspension is recorded with the correct status change.
Confirm that re-activation of a list is logged as a separate event.
Verify that deleting an exception list leaves a permanent audit record.
Ensure that exception entry submission is captured in the audit trail.
Check that approving an exception entry creates a separate audit trail record.
Verify that rejection of an exception entry is written to the audit history.
Confirm that entry edit activity is tracked even when only a single field changes.
Verify that entry suspension is logged when a user deactivates an approved entry.
Check that entry re-activation after suspension is audited separately from the original approval.
Ensure that expired entries still remain visible in the audit trail after TTL passes.
Verify that bulk upload submission creates a parent audit event.
Confirm that bulk upload approval or rejection is recorded together with the batch outcome.
Check that API submit, update, and delete events are logged with the caller identity.
Verify that every suppressed alert is logged silently without user-facing notification noise.
Confirm that suppression logging includes the watchlist, score, and screening timestamps.
Check that evidence attachment upload is recorded in the audit trail.
Verify that viewing or downloading evidence is separately logged.
Ensure that a material identity change auto-suspension event is captured.
Verify that a true-hit conflict check blocked submission is recorded as an integrity event.
Confirm that the exception register report generation is logged.
Check that exporting the audit trail to CSV is itself logged.
Verify that audit records are read-only and cannot be edited through the application.
Ensure that audit records remain searchable after the retention period is configured.
Check that the audit trail shows before and after state snapshots for state-changing actions.
Verify audit trail filters narrow results by event type, list, and date range
Verify Read-Only Auditor can view and export audit records but cannot modify them
Verify MLRO has full read access to audit records created by other users
Verify KYC Analyst sees only audit records linked to their own submissions
Verify Compliance Manager has full read access to audit records created by other users
Check that a new exception entry cannot be submitted when any mandatory field is left blank.
Verify the conditional behaviour for Original Script Name and Script Type when a non-Latin name is entered.
Create a new exception entry from list detail and route it through maker-checker approval
Use the alert-driven path and verify that the entry form is prefilled from the screening alert.
Block the submission when the customer is already present on an active Custom List or blacklist.
Check the warning path when the distinguishing evidence is too thin but the user chooses to continue.
Update an approved entry and verify that the change is sent back through the approval workflow.
Make sure an entry sitting in Pending Approval cannot be edited until the request is resolved.
Verify that scope expansion sends the edit to a higher approval level than a simple reduction.
Suspend a live entry and confirm that suppression stops as soon as the approval is completed.
Soft-delete an entry and verify that the system keeps the record for audit and history review.
Verify that the pre-expiry reminder workflow fires before the TTL runs out.
Confirm that an entry flips to Expired automatically and no longer suppresses matches once TTL has passed.
Renew an expired exception entry through maker-checker approval
Upload a clean CSV batch and verify that the import reaches the approval stage with the correct summary.
Check how the system handles a mixed file that contains both valid and invalid rows.
Verify that create, update, and delete actions received through API calls are captured in the audit trail.
Push the API request rate past the configured limit and confirm that throttling kicks in.
Save a partially completed exception entry as Draft without entering maker-checker approval
Block submission of a Draft that still has missing mandatory fields
Edit and resave a Draft entry with updated field values
Verify that invalid updates in Draft prevent successful submission.
Submit a completed Draft entry into the maker-checker approval queue
Verify IP Address/CIDR and IP Validity Period validate for IP Range exception type.
Verify Mobile Number enforces E.164 format when exception type is Mobile Number.
Verify Reason Detail enforces minimum 50 and maximum 2,000 characters.
Verify Other reason code requires 200+ chars in Reason Detail and MLRO checker routing.
Verify entry form displays correct checker routing hint for standard vs PEP/Other reason codes
Verify Re-activate for suspended entries routes through maker-checker with mandatory reason.
Verify material identity change auto-suspends entries within 15 minutes.
Verify bulk upload duplicate detection for same customer ID and watchlist scope.
Verify checker can drill into bulk upload rows before batch approval.
Verify View History panel shows submission, approval, and suppression events
Verify match score colour-coded badge in entry grid
Verify POST /csel/conflict-check blocks conflicting customer ID before submission.
Verify API bulk endpoint accepts up to 500 entries per call.
Verify KYC onboarding flagged Pending CSEL Approval on onboarding exception submit.
Verify Script Type values AR, ZH-CN, ZH-TW, CY, LA
Verify bulk suspend/delete of multiple entries is not supported
Verify Jurisdiction Scope optional field limits exception application to specified jurisdiction when populated.
Verify Email Address conditional field validates format when alert was triggered by email match.
Verify True Hit confirmed alert cannot be submitted to CSEL scope.
Verify entry can be initiated from Case Management with evidence reference linked to source case.
Verify Download Template from bulk upload returns XLSX with all mandatory columns
Verify GET /csel/{listId}/entries returns paginated filtered results for API client.
Verify GET /csel/{listId}/entries/{entryId}/audit returns full entry audit history.
Verify exception list landing page shows summary cards, status tabs, and list grid with required columns
Check that list search, filter, sort, pagination, and file export behave as a single flow on the landing screen.
Create a new exception list with valid input and verify that it is routed through the approval flow.
Confirm that mandatory fields and duplicate list names are blocked at save time.
Verify the PEP exception list rule that the default review frequency cannot exceed six months.
Open exception list detail and confirm metadata panel, entry grid, and permitted actions
Verify entry-level search, filter, sort, and export from the list detail screen.
Change the allowed fields of an existing list and send the update through approval.
Check that the list category stays locked after creation and cannot be changed during edit.
Suspend a list and verify that the system warns the user before the action is committed.
Bring back a suspended list and confirm that the earlier active entries return to use.
Delete a list through the supported soft-delete flow and verify that the reason is mandatory.
Confirm that deleted lists are retained as soft-deleted records and are not physically purged.
Verify that landing page counters recalculate correctly after entry status changes.
Verify that dashboard counters update after approval and rejection actions.
Verify that dashboard counters remain consistent after page refresh and re-login.
Verify that List Name accepts exactly 100 characters.
Verify that List Name exceeding 100 characters is rejected.
Verify that Description accepts exactly 500 characters.
Verify that Description exceeding 500 characters is rejected.
Verify landing page summary cards display Total lists, Active lists, Total exceptions, and Pending approval
Verify list status tabs (Active, Suspended, All) filter the landing grid
Verify landing grid columns include Exp 30d and Expired entry counters aligned to list detail
Verify Create Exception List supports Save as draft without entering maker-checker queue.
Verify Notify Compliance Officer and Auto-expire entries at TTL toggles persist on create form.
Verify Reason for Creation is mandatory and retained in audit log
Verify 24 months default TTL option enforces MLRO sign-off requirement
Verify pagination supports 10, 25, 50, and 100 rows per page
Verify Bulk upload is accessible from landing page header
Verify sidebar menu search filters navigation menu items.
Verify that the report opens with the correct summary cards and section layout.
Check that the total active exceptions count matches the data shown in the report table.
Verify the New This Month metric against newly created exception items.
Confirm that the Suppressions This Month metric increments when alerts are suppressed.
Check the Expiring Within 30 Days count and sample list entries.
Verify that the Entries by Reason Code breakdown is displayed with percentages.
Verify that clicking a reason code row opens the corresponding filtered view or detail context.
Check that the watchlist analysis section shows the correct top watchlist sources.
Confirm that the report export button creates a CSV file with the same visible data.
Confirm that the PDF export mirrors the report layout and includes the header information.
Verify that filters for list name or category narrow the report results correctly.
Check that status filters return the expected list states such as Active or Suspended.
Verify the page-size control so the report shows the requested number of rows.
Confirm that pagination navigates between report pages without losing the selected filters.
Check that date-related values are displayed in the expected report format.
Verify that very long list names do not break the report layout.
Check that special characters and punctuation in list names are rendered safely.
Confirm that the report handles an empty result set with a proper no-data message.
Verify that a user without report permission cannot export or view the register data.
Check that the report refreshes to show recent screening activity after new events occur.
Verify that report values are consistent across screen refresh and browser reopen.
Check that the report summary does not mix current month and historical month totals.
Confirm that the report can be opened without visible performance lag on a normal dataset.
Verify that the report header shows the correct month label and delivery context.
Check that the report keeps the visible list ordering when no sort is changed.
Verify Executive Summary includes renewals, expiries, and pending requests
Verify Suppression Activity Log groups suppressions by exception entry.
Verify Entries Expired This Month confirms suppression ceased and alerts resumed.
Verify Active Exception Entries section lists all required columns with accurate data
Verify Pending Requests section reflects outstanding maker-checker items at report generation time
Confirm that a screening hit is suppressed only when the customer ID, watchlist scope, status, and expiry checks all pass together.
Verify that a watchlist outside the configured scope does not suppress the alert even when the customer ID matches.
Confirm that a suspended exception entry is ignored during evaluation even when the rest of the data matches.
Verify that an expired exception does not suppress a new hit after the expiry date has passed.
Check the boundary case where the expiry date is exactly today and no suppression should be applied.
Ensure that a customer ID mismatch blocks suppression even when the name and watchlist appear to match.
Verify that a missing customer ID on the alert does not allow the exception to suppress the hit.
Check that a blank watchlist scope on the exception record prevents suppression.
Confirm that inactive or draft status records are ignored during evaluation.
Verify that one valid exception among multiple candidate records is enough to suppress the hit.
Confirm that the suppression event is written to audit when an alert is successfully suppressed.
Verify that a small spelling change still matches when the score stays above the configured threshold.
Confirm that a name variation below the configured threshold does not apply the exception.
Check the boundary case where the match score is exactly equal to the configured threshold.
Confirm that phonetic matching catches a sound-alike name even when the spelling is different.
Ensure that fuzzy matching never overrides an exact customer ID mismatch.
Verify that leading and trailing spaces do not break a valid fuzzy name match.
Check that a case-only difference does not stop a valid name comparison.
Confirm that punctuation changes such as hyphens or apostrophes are handled without a false negative.
Check that an inserted or missing middle name is still evaluated correctly by the matching engine.
Verify behaviour for a very long customer name so the matching logic does not fail on length.
Confirm that names containing diacritics or special characters are handled safely.
Ensure that an empty incoming name cannot be used to trigger a false suppression.
Check that a common short-form spelling does not bypass the customer ID rule.
Verify that Arabic-script names are matched correctly when the alert and the exception both carry the original script.
Verify Arabic prefix handling for names such as Al-, El-, Bin-, and Bint-.
Confirm that an Arabic-script alert does not get suppressed when the exception stores only a Latin transliteration.
Check that mixed Latin and Arabic text is stored and displayed without breaking UTF-8 handling.
Verify that Simplified Chinese names are matched exactly when both sides use the same script.
Verify that Traditional Chinese text is handled as a separate script and matched correctly when stored the same way.
Confirm that Cyrillic names are matched correctly without losing characters during processing.
Verify that the system stores and renders UTF-8 characters without corruption after evaluation.
Check that the engine uses the Latin name when the alert arrives in Latin script and the exception stores both versions.
Verify that whitespace differences in a multilingual name do not cause a false mismatch.
Ensure that a multilingual entry with multiple name representations still suppresses the hit when the correct version matches.
Check that a threshold change on the exception list immediately affects the decision outcome.
Verify that the engine selects the valid active entry when duplicate entries exist for the same customer and watchlist.
Confirm that an exception is not applied when the customer data is incomplete even though the watchlist matches.
Check that the system does not suppress a hit when the name score is close to, but still below, the threshold after normalisation.
Verify that multilingual search results remain stable after switching between screens or refreshing the page.
Verify evaluation is binary — partial criteria match never suppresses alert.
Verify that the Approve and Reject actions are not available to a user who does not have a permitted checker role for a standard CSEL request.
Confirm that a Compliance Officer can approve a standard exception request when the user holds the correct checker role.
Verify that a Compliance Manager can approve a standard request in the same way as a Compliance Officer.
Ensure that a peer analyst cannot process a request even if the user can open the queue screen.
Check that a PEP-related request can be approved only by the MLRO or a designated deputy.
Verify that an exception entry tagged with the 'Other' reason code is restricted to MLRO approval only.
Confirm that renewal of an entry older than 12 months is routed to MLRO approval.
Check that a request submitted by the logged-in user is listed under My Requests and not presented for self-approval.
Ensure that a checker cannot approve their own request even when the checker role matches the request type.
Verify that All Requests shows every pending item that is waiting for checker action.
Confirm that the queue list is refreshed after an approval so the approved item disappears from the pending view.
Verify that approving a standard request changes the workflow status to Approved and activates the exception.
Verify that rejecting a request changes its workflow state to Rejected and prevents the exception from becoming active.
Check that a rejection cannot be submitted without a clear reason or comment when the process requires justification.
Ensure that two approval attempts on the same request are not processed twice.
Verify that a rejected request cannot be moved back to pending from the checker screen without a fresh maker submission.
Verify that the onboarding SLA countdown starts from the maker submission timestamp and not from the time the request was opened.
Check that an onboarding request shows the 12-hour escalation warning before the 24-hour SLA breach.
Verify that an onboarding request crossing the 24-hour SLA produces the required escalation notification path.
Confirm that periodic re-screening and event-driven requests use the 48-hour SLA rule.
Verify the 24-hour escalation warning for periodic and event-driven requests before the 48-hour breach.
Check that escalation notifications are generated only once for the same request at the configured SLA threshold.
Ensure that a request cannot be approved by a user who is not available in the queue because of role restriction, even if the request is searchable by ID.
Verify that a request submitted by a maker is shown to the checker with the correct pending state and not auto-approved by system refresh.
Check that simultaneous approval attempts from two sessions do not create conflicting workflow states.
Verify checker approval success modal shows action, submitter, timestamp, Pending status
Verify mandatory comment modal blocks proceed without comment
Verify MC request cards show SLA timer, urgency, and escalation warning
Verify bulk upload card shows entry count and supports drill-down.
Verify PEP exception list enforces MLRO as checker for all entries at list configuration level.
Verify CSEL exception evaluation completes within 30 ms at 95th percentile.
Verify list supports up to 250,000 active entries without functional degradation.
Verify expired entries removed from evaluation within 5 minutes of expiry.
Verify soft-deleted records retained minimum 7 years.
Verify evidence attachments store SHA-256 checksum
Verify exception evaluation continues from read-optimised replica during planned maintenance window.
Verify evidence attachments encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3 minimum).
Verify diacritic normalisation applied during multilingual name matching
Verify that a new exception submission creates an immediate notification for the compliance team.
Confirm that approval of an exception entry notifies the submitting analyst without delay.
Verify that rejection of an exception entry is pushed back to the maker with the checker comment included.
Check that onboarding requests that stay pending for 12 hours trigger the escalation email to the correct stakeholders.
Verify that periodic or event-driven requests that remain pending beyond 24 hours generate the daily escalation email at 09:00.
Ensure that an entry expiring in 30 days alerts both the list owner and the compliance officer.
Confirm that the 7-day expiry warning is delivered as a second escalation, not as a duplicate of the 30-day reminder.
Verify that on the expiry date the system notifies the compliance users and clearly indicates that screening alerts are re-activated.
Check that a material identity change immediately sends an auto-suspension notification to the Compliance Officer.
Confirm that suppressed alert events do not create noisy user notifications and are only written to the audit trail.
Verify that a successful bulk upload sends only the maker-side success notification and does not notify unrelated roles.
Verify that a bulk upload with validation errors sends an immediate failure notification and exposes the error summary.
Confirm that the monthly CSEL Register Report reaches the Compliance Manager and MLRO as a PDF email attachment.
Check that a True-Hit Conflict blocking event notifies both the submitting analyst and the compliance officer immediately.
Ensure that notification timing follows the segregation-of-duties rules and not an earlier or later schedule.
Verify notification bell shows unread indicator and Mark all read clears unread styling
Verify onboarding exception notifications carry higher priority flag
Verify list suspension warns investigation team about screening alert volume increase
Verify notification delivery channels are configurable per user in system Settings
Verify that a Compliance Officer can see the full CSEL menu and all action controls required for checker operations.
Confirm that an MLRO can access all CSEL maintenance screens and handle checker decisions for PEP or other restricted cases.
Check that a Compliance Manager has unrestricted CSEL visibility and checker rights on the approved workflow screens.
Verify that a Risk Analyst is restricted to read-only list access and cannot start entry maintenance actions.
Verify that a KYC Analyst can view only their own submissions and cannot use checker functions.
Confirm that a Level 1 Investigator has the same narrow access pattern as a KYC Analyst.
Verify that a Level 2 Investigator can create and maintain entries but still cannot approve or delete a request as a checker.
Check that the System Administrator can manage lists and entries, but does not receive bulk upload permission or checker authority.
Make sure a non-checker role cannot see or use approval controls even when a pending request is opened directly.
Verify that a checker cannot approve or reject a request that was submitted from the same account.
Check that role-based permissions are refreshed correctly after logout and a different user signs in on the same workstation.
Confirm that direct API or backend approval attempts are rejected when the caller does not have checker permission.
Verify View Own restriction limits KYC Analyst and Level 1 Investigator to their own submissions
Verify role permission matrix stays consistent for all major CSEL actions across supported roles
Verify Read-Only Auditor can view all CSEL screens but cannot perform maintenance or checker actions.
Verify Read-Only Auditor has view-only access with no create, edit, delete, bulk, or checker actions.
Verify that a new exception entry cannot be submitted when the reason code field is left blank.
Check that attaching evidence does not bypass the mandatory reason code rule.
Ensure that only the configured standard reason codes can be selected for a new exception entry.
Verify that reason codes are trimmed and stored cleanly when a user pastes extra spaces around the selected value.
Confirm that the selected reason code remains intact after the record is saved and reopened.
Verify that reason code information is displayed correctly in the list view and the entry detail screen.
Check that the reason code filter narrows the list to the selected code only.
Confirm that reason codes are exported correctly to CSV and PDF outputs.
Verify that summary counts by reason code update after a new entry using the same code is approved.
Ensure that adding evidence to a draft entry does not overwrite the selected reason code.
Check that the system prompts for supporting evidence when the maker tries to continue without attaching a file.
Verify that a valid PDF evidence file uploads successfully and stays linked to the entry.
Confirm that more than one supporting document can be attached to the same entry without losing earlier files.
Verify that opening an uploaded evidence file shows the exact file that was attached.
Check that downloading the evidence file returns an intact copy with the expected filename.
Ensure that the system blocks an unsupported evidence file type during upload.
Verify that an oversized evidence file is not accepted by the upload control.
Check that filenames containing spaces, symbols, or long text are handled safely during attachment upload.
Confirm that the evidence reference opens the originating case record when the CSEL entry is created from case management.
Ensure that an invalid or unknown evidence reference cannot be saved on the entry.
Verify that an archived or deleted source case cannot be used as the evidence reference.
Check that the attachment metadata records who uploaded the file and when it was added.
Verify that uploading the same evidence file twice does not corrupt the attachment list.
Confirm that evidence stays available after page refresh and user sign-out/sign-in.
Verify that the final approved entry keeps the same reason code and evidence reference in the history view.
Ensure that replacing a draft attachment updates the final linked file instead of keeping an outdated document.
Verify Regulatory / Law Enforcement Confirmation reason code accepts TTL per regulatory instruction.
Verify five-point regulatory examination evidence set is complete on approved entry.
